content_units: Context for this plan: 90-minute kickoff on   2026-02-11  ,   14:00–15:30 Europe/Berlin  , with   engineering lead, product manager, designer, data analyst, and client stakeholder  . The agenda below is optimized to confirm scope, assign owners, identify risks, and define success metrics in one meeting.

14:00-14:10 Welcome and meeting frame   Align on purpose, outcomes, and roles   Introductions; restate project objective; confirm meeting goals; review agenda   Shared understanding of why the project exists and what this session must decide

14:10-14:25 Scope confirmation   Agree what is in scope and out of scope   Review problem statement; key user/business needs; constraints; dependencies; out-of-scope items   Draft scope statement and exclusions

14:25-14:40 Success metrics   Define how success will be measured   Discuss business KPIs; user outcomes; delivery targets; baseline data; reporting cadence   Initial success metric list with owners for validation

14:40-14:55 Roles and ownership   Clarify decision-makers and execution ownership   Map responsibilities; identify approvers; assign workstream leads; confirm communication expectations   Named owners by workstream and decision path

14:55-15:10 Risks and blockers   Surface major risks early   Review technical, delivery, design, data, stakeholder, and dependency risks; note likelihood/impact; propose mitigations   Prioritized risk list with immediate mitigation actions

15:10-15:22 Delivery approach and milestones   Align on near-term plan   Discuss phases; first milestone; required inputs; review checkpoints; client feedback moments   Agreed first milestone and next 2-3 checkpoints

15:22-15:30 Wrap-up and commitments   Lock decisions and next steps   Recap decisions; confirm open questions; restate owners and deadlines; schedule follow-up   Clear action list, unresolved items, and next meeting date
- Confirm the meeting is for decision-making, not just status sharing.
- Ask each participant to state their role in one sentence.
- “What does a successful kickoff look like for each of us by 15:30?”
- “Which decisions do we need today so the team can start execution immediately?”
- “Are there any non-negotiables from the client or business side?”
- Start with the problem to solve before discussing features.
- Capture in-scope, out-of-scope, and assumptions live.
- Resolve ambiguous requests before moving into planning.
- “What exact problem are we solving, and for whom?”
- “What is explicitly out of scope for now?”
- “What deadlines, technical constraints, or approval constraints must shape scope?”
- Define both business and delivery success.
- Separate leading indicators from final outcomes.
- “What would make the client say this project was worth doing?”
- “Which user or business outcomes matter most?”
- “What can we measure in the first 30/60/90 days?”
- “Who owns metric definition, instrumentation, and reporting?”
- Business: conversion, retention, revenue impact, cost reduction
- User: task completion, adoption, satisfaction, time saved
- Delivery: milestone hit rate, defect rate, cycle time
- Data quality: tracking coverage, reporting accuracy, dashboard availability
- Assign one clear owner per workstream.
- Clarify who recommends, who approves, and who must be consulted.
- Avoid shared ownership without a final accountable person.
- “Who owns technical feasibility and delivery planning?”
- “Who owns design decisions and user validation?”
- “Who gives final client approval on scope changes?”
-   Product manager  : scope alignment, priorities, decision log
-   Engineering lead  : technical approach, estimates, dependency/risk tracking
-   Designer  : user flows, design validation, experience quality
-   Data analyst  : success metrics, event tracking, reporting plan
-   Client stakeholder  : business alignment, approvals, escalation point
- Focus on the top 5 risks only.
- Rate each by likelihood and impact.
- Attach one mitigation and one owner to every significant risk.
- “Are any dependencies outside this team’s control?”
- “What information is still missing from the client?”
- dependency on external vendors or client inputs
- End the planning section with concrete dates or at least milestone names.
- Confirm review rhythm and artifact expectations.
- Make the first week especially clear.
- “What is the first deliverable the team will produce?”
- “What must happen in week 1 to reduce uncertainty?”
- “Which decisions require synchronous review versus async approval?”
- “What is the earliest milestone that proves momentum?”
- Milestone 4: review against success metrics readiness
- Reserve the last 8 minutes strictly for recap and owner confirmation.
- Confirm deadlines in calendar dates, not vague phrases.
- “Who owns each next action, and by when?”
- “When is the next checkpoint, and what must be ready for it?”
Use this right after the meeting in email, Slack, or your project doc.
Attendees:   Engineering Lead, Product Manager, Designer, Data Analyst, Client Stakeholder
- Ask the   client stakeholder   to validate business goals early, before detailed solution talk.
- Ask the   engineering lead   to flag feasibility concerns before owners are assigned.
- Ask the   data analyst   to challenge any success metric that cannot be measured reliably.
- Ask the   designer   to surface user-impact risks, not just UI concerns.
- Have the   product manager   act as decision recorder and timekeeper if no facilitator is assigned.
